info.title: Hall Platform API
info.description: Proposed backend contract for agreement; it is not a claim that a backend exists. The backend owns durable persistence for immutable published layout versions and occurrence mappings, pricing assignments and revisions, inventory and capacity, buyer sessions and contact verification, holds and expiry, order-line snapshots, quote breakdowns, payment attempts, tickets, and idempotency results. Server transactions must prevent a seat from being sold twice, keep general-admission capacity nonnegative, reject confirmation of expired holds, make provider callbacks idempotent, and reuse payment attempts on checkout retry. Public projections are built server-side; draft editor assets remain in admin storage. Physical tables and indexes are intentionally unspecified. Open backend/native decisions: guest mode, session TTL, token refresh, redirect/deep-link allowlist, OTP provider, fees and discounts, payment provider, ticket issuance, session restoration, payment inventory lease, and handling of late provider callbacks after expiry.

put.description: The backend validates occurrence and published-layout context, active catalog segment IDs, target IDs and GA zone kinds, and the catalog currency. It replaces the full assignment maps atomically only when If-Match and Idempotency-Key are accepted. A seated zone is expanded to explicit seat IDs by the client; GA capacity remains in the published layout. HTTP 400 reports invalid assignments, HTTP 409 reports revision/catalog/layout/idempotency conflicts, and HTTP 503 reports a possibly unknown mutation outcome that must be retried with the same body and key.

post.summary: Create an owned hold from current availability
post.description:
The server verifies the expected occurrence layoutVersionId, availabilityRevision, and pricingRevision before reserving inventory. A stale price revision returns HTTP 409 with code price_changed; refresh current prices and confirm the amount before retrying. It validates seat and general-admission availability, returns authoritative line items, total, and expiry, and commits inventory allocation and hold state atomically.

delete.summary: Cancel an owned hold and release its inventory
delete.description:
Requires If-Match with the expected hold revision returned by GET /api/v2/buyer/holds/{id}. Releases this purchase session’s hold. Replaying the same Idempotency-Key and request returns the original response. A new cancellation request for an already cancelled or expired hold is a no-op and returns 204 when it supplies that hold’s latest revision. If order conversion races with cancellation and conversion wins, the server returns 409 without cancelling the converted hold; resume the purchase session to retrieve the order.

post.summary: Create a buyer purchase session or exchange a host bootstrap credential
post.description:
Creates a guest buyer session scoped to the occurrenceId in the request or exchanges a one-time host bootstrap credential. Each widget instance gets its own purchase session and must not share its purchaseSessionId with another widget instance. Returns a non-secret purchaseSessionId selector separately from the buyer-session credential, plus its expiry. Credential transport and storage must use the approved first-party or host mechanism; this contract does not prescribe a refresh or cookie flow.

post.summary: Accept a current quote and begin server-selected payment
post.description:
Send both the expected quoteRevision and orderRevision. The backend validates the active hold, contact and verification requirements, accepts the quote, and creates or reuses one payment attempt. Order revision increments when a quote is accepted and on each checkout, payment, or order state change. Reads do not mutate revision. On HTTP 409, resume the session, read the order, compare currentRevision, then retry only after reconciling state. Inventory lease duration during external payment and treatment of a provider callback arriving after expiry remain backend integration decisions.
